function.name: calculate_Bond_Price
function.description: Calculate the bond price based on its face value, coupon rate, required rate of return, and the number of years until maturity. The calculation assumes annual coupon payments. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Face_Value.description: The nominal value or par value of the bond in dollars. This is a float type value.

Coupon_rate.description: The annual coupon rate of the bond expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

Required_return.description: The annual required rate of return for the bond investment expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

maturity_years.description: The number of whole years until the bond's maturity.

message.content:
I don’t have real‑time market data, so I can’t give you the exact spot price of gold for today.  The most reliable way to get the current U.S. gold price is to check a reputable financial news or commodities website that updates continuously, such as:

| Source | Typical update frequency | How to find the price |
|--------|--------------------------|-----------------------|
| **Kitco** | Every few minutes | Go to the “Gold” section on the homepage; the spot price is shown in USD per ounce. |
| **Bloomberg** | Every minute | Search “Gold” or “XAUUSD” in the ticker search bar. |
| **Reuters** | Every minute | Look up “Gold” under the commodities section. |
| **Investing.com** | Every minute | Search “Gold” or “XAUUSD” and view the live chart. |
| **Yahoo Finance** | Every minute | Search “Gold” or “XAUUSD” and check the “Price” field. |

If you need a quick estimate, the spot price of gold has been hovering around **$1,950–$2,000 per troy ounce** in recent weeks, but it can fluctuate by a few dollars per ounce each trading day. For the exact figure, please refer to one of the sites above or your brokerage platform.
